subject: Recap & next steps — Dedicated capacity for AuraCare
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Marc Bennett <marc.bennett@auracare.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 18:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & next steps — Dedicated capacity for AuraCare

Thanks for the conversation today, Marc — appreciate you walking us through AuraCare's current inference pain and priorities. Summarizing the main points so we’re aligned and can surface the pieces Ben/Jordan will need to validate scope on our side.

Top pain points you described:
- Unpredictable latency during peak ingest windows (metrics: 95th percentile spikes to ~1.8s for short prompt inference).
- Concerns about multi-tenancy isolation due to PHI-sensitive payloads.
- Cost uncertainty when traffic scales — need predictable unit economics for pricing models.

Primary goals for a dedicated pool:
- Strong isolation (dedicated GPU pool + VPC) with audit logs for requests for compliance.
- Throughput target: sustain ~250 qps inference (avg short prompts) with headroom for burst to 400 qps.
- SLOs: 95th percentile latency <= 300ms for production-critical routes; clear fallback plan if capacity constrained.
- Timeline: pilot in 8–10 weeks, production commitment in Q4 depending on procurement.

Immediate next steps (owner in parentheses):
1) I’ll send a one-page mutual action plan (MAP) draft and commercial estimate for a 3-month pilot (Priya) — attached draft MAP and estimate.
2) Ben to confirm sizing assumptions (model family, sequence length distribution, expected KV cache hit rate) and propose quantization profile to hit latency targets (Ben).
3) Jordan to draft an ops handoff checklist and isolation runbook (Jordan).
4) Marc to share AuraCare’s vendor security questionnaire and SOC 2 attestation if available (Marc / Procurement).

Attachments included: redwood-dedicated-estimate-v1.xlsx, auracare-map-draft.md

I’ll coordinate a 30- to 45-minute technical deep-dive next week focused on throughput/benchmarking. Proposed windows: Tue/Fri morning PT. Reply with preferred slot and if there are additional attendees from your infra/security team.

Best,

Priya Natarajan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Thanks, Priya — clear and helpful. A couple clarifications from our side:

1) The 250 qps is our baseline across three tenant shards (roughly even distribution); burst patterns typically come during morning ingest windows (08:00–10:00 PT) where we see a 2–3x multiplier for ~45 minutes.
2) Our production prompts average 320 tokens output but vary widely; a separate set of short prompts (customer-facing) are ~40–80 tokens and are what we need <300ms on.

I uploaded the vendor questionnaire — it has sections for SOC 2, data residency, and audit logs. We’ll also loop in procurement for commercial terms.

Attachment: auracare_vendor_questionnaire.pdf (PDF, 6 pages)

For scheduling the technical call, Friday morning PT (May 22, 09:00–09:45 PT) works for our infra lead, Tara (tara.jenkins@auracare.ai). Please confirm and include a runbook/benchmark plan we can review in advance.

—Marc

Marc / team — quick technical note ahead of tomorrow’s call so we can make it productive. I looked through the questionnaire and have a couple of assumptions I want to validate:

- Model family: are you planning to run a Llama2-family variant (7B/13B) or something larger? Per-token latency and KV cache size differ significantly.
- Typical sequence length for the short prompts you called out: please confirm median tokens in/ out; I’ll use 64/80 as a baseline for initial sizing if you don’t have exact metrics.
- KV cache: if you’re using session-based context (chat history) at scale, we’ll size the memory footprint differently; confirm whether per-session context retention is required across requests.

Preliminary plan to hit your SLOs: use a dedicated pool of 8xA100/GPU-equivalent nodes with mixed-precision quantization (4-bit for less-sensitive paths), continuous batching with 50–80ms batching windows for short prompts, and a prefix-KV cache to reduce repeated history decoding. I’ll validate memory and throughput numbers on prototype infra tomorrow and share revised estimate.

I attached a short benchmark checklist we’ll run in the call and a draft quantization table.

Attachments referenced: redwood-benchmark-checklist.md (text), redwood-dedicated-estimate-v1.xlsx

—Ben
